purpose: Derives a deterministic, offline-replayable audit sample, version 2 of the beacon-seeded fair-sampling family, from a caller-pasted public randomness beacon pulse (drand quicknet or NISTIR-8213) and an item-manifest hash committed before the pulse round, over the same HMAC-DRBG (SHA-256) stream as version 1 (art-583). Version 2 fixes three version 1 defects in a new node rather than editing the proven original: a threshold-rejection reduction replaces the raw modulo so index selection is exactly unbiased; a partial Fisher-Yates walk over an index array consumes exactly sample_size accepted draws with no draw cap, so full samples succeed at any population up to the 1,000,000-item ceiling (version 1's draw cap failed near-full samples above roughly 12,000 items); and both hex inputs are validated as exactly 64 lowercase hex characters, with a structured refusal otherwise. The ceiling commits to a 4 MB index array at maximum population. The emitted per-draw transcript is capped at 50 entries and carries full draws_used and rejection counts, so the artifact stays bounded while the walk remains fully reconstructible offline from the declared inputs alone. The beacon pulse is caller-declared: this kernel does SHA-256/HMAC math only, never fetches a pulse and never verifies its signature. The version 1 node stays untouched and replayable for every receipt already issued against it; new runs should use this node.
